title: LiteLLM v1.106.1 fixes count_tokens, MCP tool calls and thinking blocks
points: Bare MCP tool names on a single-server scope now go to that server, so a cold replica no longer returns `Tool not found`.
Vector stores created through the proxy send only the caller's `metadata` to the provider, so later metadata updates no longer fail with 400.
Token count responses carry `litellm_count_source`, and Anthropic-format count requests for OpenAI and Gemini models match how `/v1/messages` converts them.

title: LiteLLM v1.105.2 fixes count_tokens, bridged tool calls and thinking blocks
points: Chat completions bridged to `/responses` return text and tool calls in one `choices[0]`, so agents that read only `choices[0]` run the tool.
Signed thinking blocks with empty text stay on `/v1/messages` and chat completion requests, so replayed turns keep their reasoning.
The `v1.104.4` token count fixes are included, and count responses carry `litellm_count_source`.

title: LiteLLM v1.103.6 fixes realtime handshake errors and double spend logs
points: A refused upstream realtime handshake now sends the client an `error` event and closes with 1008, 1013 or 1011.
Non-streaming requests of 256 KiB or more on the chat to Responses bridge now log spend once instead of twice.
This patch has no new database migrations.

title: LiteLLM v1.106.0 adds Claude Haiku 5.5, a Rust Lens service and MCP rate limits
points: Claude Haiku 5.5 works on day one across Anthropic, Bedrock, Bedrock Mantle, Vertex AI, Azure AI and Perplexity.
Lens runs as a standalone Rust service, and agents upload traces to it directly with dedicated keys.
MCP Gateway rate limits now cover every MCP operation, and a new server-level `rpm` caps all callers of one server.
The caller's LiteLLM key is never forwarded to MCP servers, so each upstream server needs its own static header or OAuth credential.

title: LiteLLM v1.103.5 fixes tool calls in chat completions on GPT-5.4 and newer
points: Tool calls no longer appear on a separate `choices[1]`, so agents that read only `choices[0]` run them.
Each tool call in one non-streaming reply now gets its own `index` value instead of 0.
The fix applies to `/chat/completions` calls with tools on GPT-5.4 and newer and on `responses/` deployments.

title: LiteLLM v1.105.1 fixes SpendLogs rows and daily model usage writes
points: The model leaderboard rollup now writes `LiteLLM_DailyModelUsage` in batches, so heavy traffic to one model no longer drops SpendLogs rows.
Non-streaming requests of 256 KiB or more on the chat to Responses bridge now log spend once instead of twice.
This patch has no new database migrations and no breaking changes.

title: LiteLLM v1.104.3 adds hosted vLLM and Microsoft-Decision-1 to Decisions
points: Decisions requests that send `safety_identifier` to a provider other than OpenAI now return 400, so set `drop_params` to `true` to keep the old behavior.
The `litellm.systemone()` SDK function takes the System One format, and `litellm.decisions()` takes the OpenAI format.
The `azure_ai/` prefix serves Microsoft-Decision-1, and `hosted_vllm/` is a new Decisions provider that requires `api_base`.

title: LiteLLM v1.105.0 adds Claude Sonnet 5.5, the Decisions API and litellm.agent()
points: Claude Sonnet 5.5 works on day one across Anthropic, Bedrock, Bedrock Mantle, Vertex AI, Azure AI, OpenRouter and Perplexity.
`/v1/decisions` and `/v1/systemone` let decision models answer yes/no, choice and score questions across OpenAI, Perplexity, TypeSafe, OpenRouter and Cloudflare.
`litellm.agent()` runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Deep Agents through the AI gateway from the SDK.
Bedrock GPT-5.6, GPT-6 and GPT-6.1 use native Chat Completions, which changes response ids and reasoning fields, so use `bedrock/converse/<model>` to stay on Converse.

title: LiteLLM v1.104.2 adds Decisions API routes for OpenAI and System One
points: The proxy now serves `POST /v1/decisions` in OpenAI's Decisions API format and `POST /v1/systemone` in the System One format.
Decision models from OpenAI, Perplexity, TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Cloudflare Clef and self-hosted Strands Decider answer on both routes.
Malformed requests, such as a missing `state` or more than 128 questions, return HTTP 400 before any upstream call.

title: LiteLLM v1.102.4 fixes double-counted spend on the chat to Responses bridge
points: Since v1.102.0, large non-streaming chat requests to `openai/responses/*` models logged spend twice, and each request now logs once.
Key, team and daily spend now match the real cost of each request, and streaming requests are unchanged.

title: LiteLLM v1.101.6 fixes Codex CLI tool calls on the Responses to Chat bridge
points: Codex CLI tools now reach models behind the Responses to Chat Completions bridge, such as Bedrock Converse models.
The bridge moves `additional_tools` input items into `tools` for every bridged provider.
The model call returns to Codex as a `custom_tool_call` in both streaming and non-streaming responses.

title: LiteLLM v1.104.1, v1.103.4 and v1.102.3 update pgbouncer to 1.26.0
points: Wolfi's `openssl-dev` package now installs OpenSSL 4.0, so the Docker images bundle pgbouncer 1.26.0 to build again.
The locked Python dependencies update `langgraph-sdk` to 0.4.4, `mako` to 1.4.2 and `werkzeug` to 3.1.9.
The Admin UI updates `next` to 16.3.6 and `moment` to 2.31.0.

title: LiteLLM v1.100.5 and v1.101.5 update next to 16.3.6 and urllib3 to 2.8.0
points: The locked Python dependencies update `urllib3` to 2.8.0, `pypdf` to 6.19.0 and `pyjwt` to 2.15.0.
The Admin UI updates `next` to 16.3.6, and the wolfi-base image digest picks up glibc 2.44-r6.

title: LiteLLM v1.103.3 fixes streamed alias spend and bridged tool calls
points: The proxy exits at startup when database setup fails, unless you set `ENFORCE_PRISMA_MIGRATION_CHECK=false` to keep the old behavior.
Streamed requests through an alias such as `claude-opus-4.6` now record spend from the deployment model instead of $0.
Chat replies bridged from the Responses API now put tool calls in `choices[0]`, so clients that read only the first choice run the tool.

title: LiteLLM v1.104.0 adds Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 and master key enforcement
points: The model catalog adds 331 entries, such as Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna.
The proxy refuses to start when `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` is unset, empty or publicly known, so set a strong key before you upgrade.
An exhausted budget now returns HTTP 422 instead of 429, so set `litellm_settings.budget_exceeded_status_code: 429` to keep the old status.
stdio MCP servers are off by default, so set `LITELLM_ENABLE_MCP_STDIO=true` in the proxy environment to start them again.

title: LiteLLM v1.103.2 supports Claude Code auto mode and fixes CLI spend
points: The proxy forwards `safeguards` and `anthropic-beta` unchanged on `/v1/messages`, so Claude Code auto mode runs through the gateway.
New CLI session spend is recorded under the per-user `cli-session-<user_id>` alias instead of a 64-character session hash.
Pass-through endpoints from the config and the database merge again, and `forward_headers: true` forwards `Authorization` again.

title: LiteLLM v1.101.4 supports Straiker v3 keys and fixes Azure Content Safety
points: The Straiker guardrail calls `/api/v3/detect` for v3 platform keys, which start with `sk_agt_`.
A block from Straiker now reaches the caller as HTTP 400 with the tenant's block message.
Azure Content Safety guardrails now use `2024-09-01` when `api_version` is unset, so requests no longer return HTTP 404.

title: LiteLLM v1.103.1, v1.102.2, v1.101.3 and v1.100.4 fix UI and CLI session tokens
points: Session tokens issued before the upgrade are rejected, so Admin UI and `lite` CLI users must run `lite login` again.
Session tokens now use AES-256-GCM with their own context and return as `litellm_login_` followed by unpadded base64url.
Login tokens no longer start with `sk-`, so the proxy no longer returns HTTP 401 for about one login in 262,144.

title: LiteLLM v1.103.0 adds Fuse V2, TypeSafe Jev and config file ownership
points: The proxy now ignores database values for keys in `config.yaml` and returns 400 on runtime writes, so edit the file and restart.
Fuse V2 routing now runs after the capability forecast, and per-model Fast mode is available.
Without a license, the proxy allows one Capability router and one Fuse v2 router, and a second router returns 403.
The catalog adds 408 models from providers such as AIHubMix, Azure, Together AI and Vertex AI, and corrects the price of 147 models.

title: LiteLLM v1.100.3 fixes GPT-6 request rules and end-user budget resets
points: GPT-6 names such as `gpt-6-astra` now get the GPT-5 request rules, so chat completions accept `reasoning_effort`, `max_tokens` and function tools.
The end-user budget reset now zeroes the cached spend counter in memory and Redis, so customers no longer get 429 errors.
Shared end-user budgets with more than about 32,700 customers now reset, because the job resets end users by budget link.
